slides.title: Plant or fungus?
slides.newHtml:
Plant or fungus?

Plants
  • Cell wall: cellulose
  • Carbohydrate store: starch
  • Nutrition: photosynthesis (chloroplasts)
Fungi
  • Cell wall: chitin
  • Carbohydrate store: glycogen
  • Nutrition: saprotrophic (external enzymes)
⚠ EXAMINER TRAP: Fungi NEVER have chloroplasts and NEVER photosynthesise!

slides.title: Pathogens and diseases
slides.oldHtml:
Pathogens and diseases

Fungi
  • Trichophyton → athlete’s foot
  • Candida → thrush
  • Diplocarpon → rose black spot
Bacteria
  • ★ Pneumococcus → pneumonia
  • Vibrio cholerae → cholera
  • Salmonella → food poisoning
  • Mycobacterium → TB
Protoctists
  • ★ Plasmodium → malaria
  • Entamoeba → amoebic dysentery
  • Phytophthora → potato blight
Viruses (not a kingdom)
  • ★ Influenza → flu · ★ HIV → AIDS
  • ★ Tobacco mosaic virus → leaf mottling
  • Measles virus → measles
★ Named in the Edexcel IGCSE specification · Animals and plants are not microbial pathogens (though mosquitoes act as vectors).

slides.title: Viruses
slides.oldHtml:
Viruses

NOT ALIVE · NOT A KINGDOM
  • Not made of cells
  • Genetic material (DNA or RNA) inside a protein coat
  • Much smaller than bacteria
  • Parasites: only reproduce inside living cells
  • Infect every kind of organism
  • e.g. flu, HIV, tobacco mosaic virus

slides.title: Are viruses living cells?
slides.newHtml:
Are viruses living cells?

Which statement about viruses is TRUE?
AThey are tiny prokaryotic cells with a cell wall
BThey are not cells — just a protein coat + DNA or RNA
CThey reproduce independently on food surfaces
⚠ EXAMINER TIP: Viruses are parasitic — they can ONLY reproduce inside living host cells!

slides.title: Which transport process?
slides.newHtml:
Which transport process?

1. O₂ into blood
Oxygen moves from high concentration in alveoli to low in blood
→ DIFFUSION
Passive (no energy)
2. Mineral ions into roots
Ions move from low concentration in soil to high inside root hair cells
→ ACTIVE TRANSPORT
Uses energy (respiration)
3. Water into plant cells
Water moves across a partially permeable membrane from dilute to concentrated
→ OSMOSIS
Water ONLY!
⚠ EXAMINER TRAP: Osmosis is ALWAYS water only — never sugar or mineral ions!

slides.title: Exam question [4]
slides.oldHtml:
Exam question [4]

Ben waters his plant with salt water by mistake. Explain why the plant wilts.
Salt water has a low water potential · water moves out of the plant cells · from high to low water potential · across a partially permeable membrane · by osmosis · cells become flaccid / plasmolysed · plant wilts

Exam question [4]

slides.title: Spot the exam traps!
slides.newHtml:
Spot the exam traps!

Trap 1: Energy wording
✗ "Respiration produces / makes energy"
✓ Respiration RELEASES energy from glucose (energy cannot be created!)
Trap 2: Breathing ≠ Respiration
✗ "Respiration means breathing air in and out"
✓ Breathing = ventilation in the lungs. Respiration = chemical reaction in every living cell!

Heart and lungs can’t supply enough oxygen · less aerobic respiration / ATP · more anaerobic respiration · more lactic acid · can cause cramp
